question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own the ClawHub-specific publisher-feed protocol, trust policy, scheduler, and shared SQLite state, or should core expose a generic signed-feed seam while ClawHub or an official plugin owns this workflow?
rationale: Repository policy favors lean, plugin-agnostic core, while this stack introduces service-specific protocol constants, trust decisions, persistence, gateway lifecycle, RPCs, and UI follow-ups; code review cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Use a generic core seam
options.body: Keep only reusable signed-feed and storage primitives in core and move ClawHub-specific publisher policy and lifecycle into its owning plugin or service package.

options.title: Sponsor core ownership
options.body: Explicitly accept publisher feeds as a first-party core capability and review the complete stacked protocol, persistence, upgrade, gateway, and UI contract in dependency order.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Wait for the producer and RFC contracts to stabilize before accepting a permanent consumer storage and trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Use a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Keep only reusable signed-feed and storage primitives in core and move ClawHub-specific publisher policy and lifecycle into its owning plugin or service package.

likelyOwner.reason: This is principally a repository product-boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.
